DOI:10.1109/acctcs66275.2025.00098.abstract: This paper mainly discusses how to optimize the use of resources effectively through distributed management in large-scale machine learning model training and reasoning. First, this paper analyzes the challenges that traditional resource management approaches face when dealing with large models, such as compute pressure, storage requirements, and network bottlenecks. Then, a new resource optimization strategy based on distributed architecture is proposed, which utilizes dynamic load balancing, task scheduling and resource sharing technologies to improve resource utilization and system efficiency. In addition, this paper also demonstrates the application effect of the proposed strategy in different scenarios through case analysis and experimental verification, and proves its advantages in reducing cost, shortening training time and improving model performance.

DOI:10.1109/acsosc56246.2022.00018.abstract: In this paper, we explore the use of Reinforcement Learning (RL) to improve the control of cooling equipment in Data Centers (DCs). DCs are inherently complex systems, and thus challenging to model from first principles. Machine learning offers a way to address this by instead training a model to capture the thermal dynamics of a DC. In RL, an agent learns to control a system through trial-and-error. However, for systems such as DCs, an interactive trial-and-error approach is not possible, and instead, a high-fidelity model is needed. In this paper, we develop a DC model using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) based on the Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) algorithm. The model features transient boundary conditions for simulating the DC room, heat-generating servers, and Computer Room Air Handlers (CRAHs) as well as rejection components outside the server room such as heat exchangers, compressors, and dry coolers. This model is used to train an RL agent to control the cooling equipment. Evaluations show that the RL agent can outperform traditional controllers and also can adapt to changes in the environment, such as equipment breaking down.

DOI:10.1109/admit67050.2025.11337052.abstract: Brain tumor segmentation using multi-modal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is crucial for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning. However, it remains challenging due to tumor heterogeneity, the frequent absence of modalities in real-world settings, and the limited performance of existing methods in segmenting small lesions. To address these issues, we propose an adaptive mixture-of-experts model that incorporates dynamic Mamba-based scanning for robust glioma segmentation. The framework is built upon a 3D U-Net backbone, where the encoder employs a 3D Mamba mechanism for adaptive cross-modal contextual scanning, and the decoder utilizes a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) structure to enhance multiscale feature representation. To evaluate generalizability, we introduce Brats Mixing, a comprehensive multi-domain dataset integrating BraTS data from 2018 to 2023. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms Swin-Unet3D and 3DTransUNet, improving the average Dice score by 1.93 % and 2.25 %, and reducing the average 95 % Hausdorff Distance by 25.7 % and 20.7 %, respectively. The results confirm the robustness and accuracy of our approach, particularly in handling small tumors and missing modalities.

DOI:10.1109/africon66545.2025.11533824.abstract: Digital twins are increasingly deployed from the cloud down to the edge of industrial equipment, including wind-turbine nacelles, battery packs, drones, and medical wearables. In these settings, forecasting models must look hours or days into the future while running on microcontrollers with milliwatt-level power budgets. Traditional sequence models such as LSTMs or Transformers can achieve high predictive accuracy, but typically require computationally intensive back-propagation on GPUs and rely on dense floating-point arithmetic that exceeds the constraints of typical edge platforms. Furthermore, purely data-driven models may produce physically implausible forecasts, for example negative state of charge, rotor speeds above cut-out limits, or temperature discontinuities that violate basic thermodynamic constraints. This work proposes an alternative approach that is both computationally efficient and rule-consistent. We replace the usual floating-point reservoir (Extreme Learning Machine or Echo State Network) with a discrete Cellular Neural Network (dCeNN): a two-dimensional lattice of binary cells that update through local bit-wise interactions with their neighbours. To enforce physical and safety requirements, we automatically discover symbolic rules from data and encode them using Answer Set Programming (ASP). The resulting pipeline trains in under two seconds on a laptop CPU, streams thousands of forecasts per second on a Raspberry Pi, and, in preliminary experiments, does not violate any mined rule over months-long test runs (early results, work in progress).

DOI:10.1109/agro-geoinformatics70621.202.abstract: Substation localization over city-scale remote sensing imagery is bottlenecked by two unresolved challenges: the absence of large-scale oriented bounding box (OBB) datasets that treat complete substation installations as independent detection targets, and the prohibitive inference latency of processing hundreds of square kilometers of high-resolution imagery through conventional serial CPU-GPU workflows where preprocessing and inference stages alternate with substantial idle periods. We address both gaps through three integrated contributions. First, we construct a substation OBB dataset covering 119 cities across all urban tiers in China—from first-tier megacities to third-tier regional centers—comprising 7,031 positive image tiles annotated with four-corner oriented bounding boxes and verified through a dual-independent cross-validation protocol with third-party arbitration. Images are sourced from Google Earth and Tianditu at resolutions finer than 0.5 m/pixel, ensuring that critical structural features including perimeter walls, main transformers, highvoltage frameworks, and incoming/outgoing line corridors are clearly discernible. An additional 700 negative samples without substations are incorporated to suppress false positives arising from visually similar structures such as industrial complexes and large buildings in complex urban backgrounds. Second, adopting YOLOv11-OBB without any architectural modification as a fixed detection backbone, we systematically quantify through ablation experiments the individual contributions of three training components: Mosaic data augmentation for enriching sample diversity, pre-trained weight initialization for transferring low-level visual representations, and negative sample incorporation for reducing false positive detections. The full-strategy configuration achieves $98.82\% \text{mAP}{@}50$ and $85.46\% \text{mAP}{@}50:95$, establishing a transparent and reproducible strong baseline. Third, we design a Ray-based CPU/GPU asynchronous parallel inference pipeline that decouples image tiling, batched model inference, and result merging into three overlapping stages with cross-image pipeline parallelism. A distributed Actor pool manages dynamic GPU task scheduling, while CPU cores continuously preprocess subsequent images to hide data preparation latency behind computation. Experiments on 503 high-resolution images ($20,000 \times 20,000$ pixels each) covering Jiayuguan City demonstrate that the proposed heterogeneous pipeline reduces total inference time from 8.5 hours to 1.7 hours—a $5.01 \times$ end-to-end speedup over singleGPU serial execution, and a 4.17× further improvement over four-GPU data-parallel inference—with an average per-image processing time of 12.19 seconds. Resource utilization profiling reveals approximately fourfold improvement in CPU utilization and a 50 -percentage-point increase in average GPU utilization relative to the serial baseline. The dataset and inference methodology provide both data foundations and technical support for automated, city-scale substation monitoring.

DOI:10.1109/aiahpc66801.2025.11290594.abstract: Optimizing assembly correlation processes helps firms improve product quality and productivity without substantial cost increases, yet accurate prediction of assembly precision remains a key challenge in assembly manufacturing. To address this, this study proposes AAPformer (Assembly Accuracy Prediction Transformer), a neural network model developed for the practical application of UAV folded rudder wing assembly. The model can effectively capture long-range part assembly dependencies and predict final assembly accuracy, with two core improvements: an advanced position encoding technique to capture the geometric details of assembled parts in spatial positions, and a refined self-attention mechanism to efficiently handle long-distance dependencies and enhance model performance. A novel Part Assembly Relevance Dataset (PARD) is constructed using UAV rudder wing measurement data, which supports comparative experiments and ablation studies. Rigorous tests on PARD and multiple public datasets show that AAPformer achieves significantly higher accuracy than mainstream models, confirming its superior performance and strong scalability for larger, more complex datasets.

DOI:10.1109/aibdf67964.2025.11440786.abstract: This paper presents BRS-MLEGCN, a predict-then-fuse framework that combines a Biaffine Relation Scorer (BRS) with a Multi-Layer Enhanced graph convolutional network (MLEGCN) for sentiment understanding at the sentence/document level and the aspect level. The method begins with a Biaffine Relation Scorer that assigns arc and relation probabilities to form a soft dependency graph, which is then modeled by a Multi-Layer Enhanced graph convolutional network (GCN) with multi relation aggregation, residual stacking, and edge drop regularization. In parallel, a semantic branch based on a MambaFormer encoder captures short range patterns with multi head attention and long range context with a selective state space block. A Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN) gated fusion performs position wise weighting to combine graph and semantic streams into a unified representation. The formulation is task agnostic and handles both sentence classification and aspect based sentiment analysis (ABSA) by supplying the aspect span. Experiments on Internet Movie Database (IMDb) and SemEval 2014 Restaurant and Laptop show consistent improvements over strong graph based and attention based baselines, and further gains when coupled with a pretrained encoder. Ablation studies confirm that soft dependency scoring, enhanced graph propagation, and gated fusion each contribute complementary benefits, while case studies illustrate robust alignment between aspects and distant opinion cues. The framework is practical and interpretable with controllable sparsity and meaningful gate and edge attributions.

DOI:10.1109/aicas59952.2024.10595886.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have attained remarkable achievements in multi-domain tasks. However, LLMs’ performance is limited by hardware conditions due to billions of parameters. It requires highly efficient deployment and software hardware co-optimization such as quantization, pruning and operator fusion methods. Meanwhile, there is an emerging trend that LLMs run on edge devices like Arm-based CPUs. DOI:10.1109/aicas64808.2025.11173114.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) face storage and access limitations during development, requiring extensive reads of key-value (KV) cache data for each token generation. This paper designs a hardware-friendly lossless compression and decompression method for KV cache based on Token-level Redundancy Elimination and Bit-level Encoding (TREBE), reducing the amount of KV cache data that needs to be stored. In detail, token-level redundancy is first eliminated by performing subtraction between the same layers of different tokens, followed by bit-level encoding using XOR and bit-plane techniques. TREBE achieves an average compression ratio of 2.1x for the KV cache of LLaMA2-7B and OPT-6.7B models on the WikiText2 and C4 datasets, representing a 1.9x improvement over Huffman coding. With the support of TSMC 28nm process, TREBE operates at 0.9V and 0.8GHz, achieving a throughput of 6.38GB/s. Compared to Huffman coding, energy efficiency is improved by 10x, and area efficiency is enhanced by 31.2x.

DOI:10.1109/aiea70743.2026.11632615.abstract: Sweeping all beam candidates at mmWave is costly in time and spectrum. Side information like user position, partial measurements, and prior beam records can help, but these sources degrade unpredictably in the field. Existing fusion methods have no way to detect when an input has become unreliable. Our solution, RG-SMoE, gives each modality a dedicated classifier whose prediction confidence serves as a quality indicator. A peaked output suggests the modality carries real information; a flat output suggests it does not. We multiply each modality's learned representation by this quality score, suppressing the questionable ones, then pass everything through cross-attention and a sparse bank of six expert networks (two selected per sample). Evaluation used DeepMIMO O1 ray-tracing channels, 28 GHz, 128-beam codebook, 20k users. All four models trained on the same degraded data to eliminate procedural bias. Across three training runs with different seeds, RG-SMoE achieved the highest mean clean accuracy (88.9%) and ranked first or tied for first in 6 out of 9 test conditions (1 clean + 8 degradation), with the lowest run-to-run variance among all models. At ${5 0 \%}$ modality missingness, it led by 0.7 points $({7 3. 8 \%}$ vs ${7 3. 1 \%}$) with the smallest standard deviation (±0.4%). Ablations confirmed that reliability alignment and sparse routing each contribute to missingness robustness, while auxiliary supervision ensures the reliability scores remain interpretable. The per-modality quality scores also function as a runtime health check, flagging sensor problems without requiring beam ground truth.

DOI:10.1109/aiiot68874.2026.11569581.abstract: Selecting an appropriate base large language model (LLM) for deployment is increasingly challenging because model quality is multi-dimensional and application dependent. Beyond benchmark scores, practitioners must consider responsiveness (time-to-first-token), throughput under load, reasoning accuracy, conversational quality, and safety behavior. This paper presents a controlled empirical study of six open-weight LLMs (LLaMA 3.1 8B, Mistral 7B, Qwen 2.5 14B, GPT-OSS 20B, Gemma 2 27B, and Yi 34B) evaluated under identical infrastructure conditions using Ollama on an AWS g5.12xlarge instance (4x A10G). We report multi-day averaged results for streaming latency and throughput across concurrency levels up to 64, and complement system metrics with GSM8K accuracy, Alpaca-Eval-based conversational preference (LLM-as-a-Judge), and Real-Toxicity-Prompts safety analysis. Results show that no single model dominates across all axes; therefore, "the best" model must be selected with respect to downstream requirements. We conclude with an application-aware model selection framework and a routing architecture for multi-model deployments.

DOI:10.1109/aiiot68874.2026.11569636.abstract: Agentic AI in IoT must convert open-ended user requests into plans/actions for an environment whose topology, firmware, and behaviour change over time. The classical single-loop LLM tool-use designs fail in this setting due to the context window limits and the resulting limitations in reasoning, tool selection, and execution performance. We introduce and evaluate the separation of identity, capability, governance, planning, and execution into explicit layers that are fully integrated. We also introduce a three-layer manifest format and a federated rendezvous protocol. The P2P rendezvous protocol enables FerrousFeline instances to discover, verify, and reuse plans, rules, tools, observers, and experience artifacts from other instances. Each FerrousFeline instance has its own acceptance control. The evaluations show that artifacts are shared efficiently between FerrousFeline instances and that this sharing improves the capabilities of each participating instance. These results support the feasibility of manifest-mediated artifact distribution, while full multi-instance federation and cross-network behaviour remain future work.

DOI:10.1109/aim65483.2026.11658144.abstract: Robotic manipulation in complex scenes requires robust reasoning and fine-grained part-level control. While recent language-guided policies have demonstrated strong manipulation capabilities, most existing benchmarks lack explicit obstacles and other sources of interference, and do not provide corresponding obstacle-aware solutions. To address this, we introduce MOBInstruct, a benchmark for part-level manipulation in cluttered environments with obstacles, along with a hierarchical framework, MOBA, for obstacle-aware execution. The MOBA framework consists of high-level modules for task planning and scene reasoning, as well as low-level modules for part-level action execution with position-aware noise initialisation. Within our framework, we evaluate representative baselines on the MOBIn-struct benchmark. Experiments demonstrate effective obstacle removal and robust task completion in multi-object scenes under diverse environmental conditions, including lighting and tabletop textures. DOI:10.1109/aiotc71250.2026.11689468.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures have become a prevalent paradigm for scaling large language models, yet their sparse routing mechanisms introduce unique security risks: safety alignment tends to concentrate in a small subset of experts, creating a structural vulnerability. Existing backdoor methods against MoE models typically follow a data-driven paradigm, embedding malicious logic in model weights through data poisoning and fine-tuning, which leaves them susceptible to weight-based defenses. In this paper, we introduce an architectural backdoor that hard-codes detection and intervention logic directly into the model's computation graph, decoupling the backdoor from model weights. We design a handcrafted arithmetic punctuation trigger that can be injected without altering semantic content and detected via mathematical methods. Upon trigger detection, we intervene in the routing process by suppressing pre-identified safety experts, redirecting tokens toward non-safety experts to enable jailbreak outputs. We evaluate our method on seven mainstream MoE models across three safety benchmarks. Experimental results show that our approach achieves up to 96.0% jailbreak success rate with improvements of up to 47 percentage points over the baseline. The backdoor persists under full-model fine-tuning, outperforming the data-driven BadSwitch method by up to 65 percentage points under identical conditions. Ablation studies further validate that precise safety-expert localization is essential for effectiveness. Our work highlights a supplychain security risk in MoE architectures, where architecturallevel computation graph modifications can introduce persistent backdoors that evade conventional defenses.

DOI:10.1109/apr59189.2023.00013.abstract: Bug fixing is one of the most time-consuming and resource-intensive tasks in the software development life cycle. Automated Program Repair (APR) might be able to help in this process, but it still has to overcome many obstacles. Deep learning models have shown promise for automated program repair in recent years, but their effectiveness can depend on the representation of the source code used as input. In this paper, we conduct an experimental study to compare the performance of deep learning models on two popular programming languages, Java and JavaScript, using three different code representations: raw text, command sequences, and abstract syntax trees (ASTs). We also experiment with varying models, including T5, CodeT5, (for solving sequence-to-sequence tasks) RoBERTa, and GPTNeo (to encode/decode AST graph information). We evaluate the models on a set of real-world defects from open-source projects and compare the performance, and the repair patches generated by the models. Our results show that training on command sequence representation outperforms most other configurations. We achieve a best of 19.88% accuracy on the java-small dataset, and 11.87% on java-medium, using text representation. Using command sequence representation, we achieve 30.64% on java-small and 18.53% on the medium dataset. However, when representing the source with ast+text information, our models significantly underperform compared to other representations, achieving results below one percent. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of the strengths and limitations of deep learning models for automated program repair and provide practical guidance for their use in practice.

DOI:10.1109/apsec66846.2025.00018.abstract: In aerospace engineering, ensuring system safety mandates the formal verification of requirements. Propositional Projection Temporal Logic (PPTL) is a critical formalism for this purpose, enabling the precise specification of complex temporal behaviors and state-based constraints for automated model checking. However, converting natural language (NL) requirements into PPTL is a significant challenge, as Large Language Models (LLMs) often produce unreliable outputs due to inherent non-determinism and hallucination. To overcome this, we propose a hierarchical hybrid-intelligence architecture that systematically mitigates these LLM weaknesses. Our framework orchestrates collaboration through three core mechanisms: Consensus and Debate to filter errors, Authoritative Reflection by a expert model (GPT-4o) to ensure logical correctness, and a Closed-Loop Self-Correction cycle driven by actionable feedback. The system is further enhanced with Knowledge-Augmented InContext Learning from a curated aerospace knowledge base. On a dataset of real-world aerospace requirements, our framework increased the accuracy of NL-to-PPTL conversion from a 69.4 % baseline to $\mathbf{8 8. 4 \%}$.In addition, $\mathbf{2, 0 0 0}$ pieces of data were randomly selected in an open source synthetic data set, and our accuracy reached 92.9%. By emulating an expert ‘propose-review-correct’ workflow, our architecture effectively constrains LLMs for reliable application in high-stakes formal methods, paving a scalable path toward safer system development.

DOI:10.1109/asp-dac66049.2026.11420692.abstract: Circuit verification constitutes a significant bottleneck in modern electronic design, often consuming up to 70% of the development cycle due to the escalating complexity of circuits. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) presents a promising new frontier, demonstrating profound capabilities in code generation, debugging, and automated reasoning. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of LLM-assisted hardware verification. We systematically review state-of-the-art approaches that leverage LLMs for critical verification tasks, including assertion synthesis, testbench generation, automated debugging, and the development of collaborative verification frameworks. We analyze the effectiveness of various LLM strategies specifically designed for hardware verification applications, while also discussing the integration of LLMs with existing verification workflows and tools. Furthermore, the paper identifies key remaining challenges and outlines a forward-looking perspective on future research directions.

DOI:10.1109/bdai70753.2026.11655175.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently been used as frozen backbones for time-series forecasting, aiming to transfer general sequence priors through prompts and embedding-based interfaces. However, recent evidence suggests that many LLM-based forecasting pipelines do not reliably benefit from the language model itself, raising a fundamental question: under what design constraints does a frozen LLM provide measurable and attributable value for numerical time series prediction. Thus, we present Align-TS, a modular framework that makes the role of the frozen LLM explicit and testable by separating structure learning from semantic conditioning. First, a structure-guided encoder models inter-variable dependencies by operating attention over variable tokens, producing representations that preserve multivariate structure. Second, a languagespace recasting module converts structure-aware patches into embeddings that are compatible with the frozen LLM without requiring backbone updates. Third, an alignment-driven conditioning module produces task-aware prompt representations and aligns them with numerical embeddings to reduce entanglement and stabilize inference. This design yields a controllable pathway in which the LLM functions as a semantic conditioner rather than a monolithic predictor. Experiments on multiple public multivariate time-series forecasting benchmarks demonstrate that Align-TS achieves competitive and often superior forecasting performance across diverse domains while keeping the language model fully frozen.

DOI:10.1109/bibm55620.2022.9995324.abstract: Molecule property prediction based on computational strategy plays a key role in the process of drug discovery and design, such as DFT. Yet, these traditional methods are time-consuming and labour-intensive, which can’t satisfy the need of biomedicine. Thanks to the development of deep learning, there are many variants of Graph Neural Networks (GNN) for molecule representation learning. However, whether the existed well-perform graph-based methods have a number of parameters, or the light models can’t achieve good grades on various tasks. In order to manage the trade-off between efficiency and performance, we propose a novel model architecture, CoAtGIN, using both Convolution and Attention. On the local level, k-hop convolution is designed to capture long-range neighbour information. On the global level, besides using the virtual node to pass identical messages, we utilize linear attention to aggregate global graph representation according to the importance of each node and edge. In the recent OGB Large-Scale Benchmark, CoAtGIN achieves the 0.0933 Mean Absolute Error (MAE) on the large-scale dataset PCQM4Mv2 with only 5.6 M model parameters. Moreover, using the linear attention block improves the performance, which helps to capture the global representation.

DOI:10.1109/bibm62325.2024.10822624.abstract: Biomedical information extraction, including tasks like Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Relationship Extraction (RE), plays a critical role in analyzing unstructured biomedical data, facilitating more accurate downstream applications such as clinical decision support and personalized medicine. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in various domains, they often struggle with issues like hallucinations and domain-specific inaccuracies, limiting their effectiveness in biomedical applications. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel framework that incorporates an external dual-stage verifier to enhance biomedical information extraction. This verifier is prompted to first identify and complete missing entities and relations, and then filter out incorrect extractions, thereby enhancing both precision and recall in information extraction. Furthermore, we proposed an approach for constructing the instruction-tuning dataset using both positive and negative demonstrations, which improves the verifier’s correction capabilities through Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT). Our extensive experiments on three public benchmark datasets cover both biomedical NER and RE tasks, comparing four LLMs ranging from 7 to 175 billion parameters to validate the effectiveness and scalability of our approach. The results demonstrate that by integrating an external verifier specifically finetuned for biomedical tasks, we achieve substantial improvements in precision, recall, and F1 scores for NER and RE tasks. Our method consistently outperforms In-Context Learning (ICL) approaches in F1 scores, achieving increases of up to 20% in some cases. Furthermore, ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of both stages in the verification process. The proposed framework provides valuable insights for accurate biomedical information extraction using LLMs, highlighting its potential applications in real-world clinical settings.

DOI:10.1109/bibm66473.2025.11356365.abstract: Inferring the proportion of cell types present in each spatial location from a mixture of expression profiles in spatial transcriptome (ST) data is a crucial task. However, on the one hand, existing methods adopt static or predefined neighborhood structures for ST data, which limits their ability to adapt to complex spatial organization. On the other hand, existing models often rely on overly simplified linear hybrid models and fail to effectively capture spatial dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose a new deconvolution framework called NSAMTG. Specifically, we utilize the Native Sparse Attention transformer with kernel mean matching (KMM) to reduce the distribution difference of the data and perform encoding reconstruction on single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. At the same time, we build a Mixed-Topology graph transformer VAE that combines an adaptive adjacency matrix and a static adjacency matrix to capture spatial expression correlations and spatial relationships in ST data. Finally, we employ a Generative Adversarial Network with a FourierKAN discriminator to learn the complex, non-linear cell-to-spot mapping relationship and achieve cell type deconvolution. Experiments on both simulated datasets and real datasets show that our method is superior to the existing methods, opening up new possibilities for robust and zeneralizable spatial deconvolution in diverse biological contexts.

DOI:10.1109/bigdata62323.2024.10825478.abstract: Mobility scooters are popular among people with limited mobility, providing convenient transportation in their communities and thus enhancing their life quality. However, due to various reasons, a high number of mobility scooter accidents have been reported. In this paper, we tackle its safety issues by performing riding behavior stability analysis using both video and motion sensor data. We design a transformer-based cross-modal encoder to generate the embeddings representing the riding stability and develop a binary classifier based on the embeddings to classify riding behaviors as stable or unstable. The advantage of this work is that the multimodal contrastive learning approach enables the neural network to understand the correlations across two modalities for the same events, and to distinguish the unstable riding behaviors from stable, so that incontext stability analysis becomes possible. We have conducted extensive experiments based on real-world mobility scooter riding data labeled by medical practitioners. The results have shown a high level of classification accuracy of our system, across different settings, in ablation study as well as comparative study.

DOI:10.1109/bigdia60676.2023.10429210.abstract: This study examines key characteristics of cloud computing technology within the domain of federated learning, with the primary objective of exploring the principles concerning distributed computing acceleration ratio and storage input/output efficiency across various network segments. Combining the heterogeneous characteristics of cloud segments, we present a novel approach for distributed model training strategies by using the federated learning technique. This approach can keep the accuracy of the model, enhance training efficiency, and protect user privacy. The experiment demonstrates that the proposed strategy outperforms the baseline method, which does not account for variations in different segments.

DOI:10.1109/cac63892.2024.10865276.abstract: Accurately predicting photovoltaic (PV) power generation is crucial for energy companies to plan and conduct safety assessments. However, existing model-based methods are limited by low prediction accuracy, while data-driven methods also suffer from low accuracy due to the difficulty in extracting time series features from raw data. To address these issues, we developed a method based on improved moving average decomposition, which achieves short-term PV power generation prediction by integrating Unscented Kalman Filtering and an extended long short-term memory network (xLSTM). First, we used an exponentially weighted moving average method to decompose the data into seasonal and trend components, specifically modeling the trend component using a double exponential model. Second, the xLSTM consists of two improved LSTM modules, sLSTM and mLSTM, which enhance storage decision-making capabilities and storage capacity, respectively, and enable parallelization. Finally, through PV power generation prediction experiments, the results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy, with an R2 prediction result reaching 97%.

DOI:10.1109/cac63892.2024.10865303.abstract: Transformer bushings play a crucial role in power systems. Despite their importance, there has been limited research specifically on the state prediction of transformer bushings. Moreover, currently available models only predict univariate data of bushings without considering the physical connection to other relevant data, which would give rise to a compromised prediction. To achieve a more accurate joint prediction of three critical transformer states: dielectric loss, end shield current, and equivalent capacitance, this work builds upon the state-of-the-art predictive network Crossformer. In addition to Crossformer, a data generation model named TimeVAE is introduced to enlarge the scale of the training dataset. This combination enabled us to achieve accurate multivariate predictions for transformer bushings. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed predictor, we conducted comparative experiments with attention-based frameworks (Autoformer, Pyraformer, Informer, Reformer, Transformer), which are considered efficient for multivariable prediction tasks. The results show that our proposed model outperforms these models in four key metrics: mean square error, mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and coefficient of determination.

DOI:10.1109/cacml64929.2025.11010943.abstract: The field of multi-skill dialogue generation focuses on creating conversational agents capable of handling a variety of tasks. Traditional approaches, such as task detection and adapter fusion, have faced challenges; task detection heavily depends on accurate context recognition, while adapter fusion methods often suffer from high computational complexity and are constrained by the performance of single-adapter models. To address these issues, we propose a novel method called Knowledge Synergy Complement (KSC) learning for enhancing multi-skill dialogue generation. In KSC, we leverage single-skill adapters by defining their Lipschitz constants as macro knowledge and utilizing intermediate hidden states to capture micro knowledge. This complementary approach allows for better integration of diverse skills. Moreover, a novel knowledge pruning mechanism is introduced to prevent knowledge forgetting and reduce conflict between skills. Our experiments demonstrate that KSC effectively integrates multiple skills, achieving superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art methods, while also being more efficient in terms of computational and storage resources required.

DOI:10.1109/cai68641.2026.11536235.abstract: There has been substantial and growing industry demand to deploy Large Language Models (LLMs) as decision-support tools, for automation pipelines, and in AI frameworks. Nevertheless, their behavior in production settings is largely underexplored, and failure patterns are fundamentally different from their traditional machine learning predecessors. In this paper, we develop an in-depth system-level taxonomy of fifteen hidden failure modes occurring in practical LLM applications, such as multi-step reasoning drift, latent inconsistency, context-boundary degradation, incorrect tool invocation, version drift, and cost-driven performance collapse. With this taxonomy at hand, we examine the growing divide between evaluation practices and monitoring: as it stands, benchmarks are designed to evaluate knowledge or reasoning but can say very little about stability, reproducibility, drift, or ease of workflow integration. We then discuss the operational issues of deploying LLMs—such as lack of observability, cost considerations, and update-induced regressions—and propose high-level principles for designing reliable, maintainable, and cost-effective LLM systems. Finally, we sketch high-level design guidelines that can inform the construction of reliable, maintainable, and cost-aware LLM-based systems. Implicitly considering LLM reliability more as a system-engineering issue than an isolated modeling problem, the present work offers an analytical footing for upcoming research on evaluation methodology and AI system robustness and dependable LLM deployment.

DOI:10.1109/cai68641.2026.11536604.abstract: Modern Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) increasingly employ ensemble learning to capture heterogeneous attack behaviors. However, conventional Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures can overfit when the gating network is trained on the same samples used to fit the experts, leading to in-sample shortcutting and brittle routing. We introduce Validation-Gated MoE (VG-MoE), a simple training-protocol change in which experts are learned on the training split. At the same time, the gate is fitted only on out-of-sample predictions computed over a held-out validation set. This decoupling mitigates information leakage, promotes genuine expert specialization, and yields more stable routing at test time. We evaluated VG-MoE on two widely used cybersecurity benchmarks, NSL-KDD and CICIDS17, under standard class-imbalance settings. Across both datasets, VG-MoE improves overall detection accuracy relative to the strongest individual experts (base learners). Using common metrics (MacroF1, WeightedF1, and Overall Accuracy (OA)), our results indicate that separating gate training from expert fitting enhances sensitivity to rare attacks while maintaining competitive inference cost, since gating operates on low-dimensional expert logits rather than raw features. Overall, VG-MoE provides a practical, architecture-agnostic enhancement to IDS that improves accuracy without adding substantive complexity.

DOI:10.1109/cbase67452.2025.11335478.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by breaking the sequential token-bytoken generation constraint. This technique uses draft models to generate multiple candidate tokens, which are then validated by target models. While EAGLE-3 represents the current state-of-the-art method through multi-layer hidden state fusion and training-time test, it faces significant engineering and efficiency limitations. The method requires access to intermediate layer features from target models, making it intrusive to existing inference frameworks and challenging to deploy. Additionally, the complex computational graph needed for training-time test results in inefficient training processes. We introduce KVSpec, which reuses KV cache that is available during any LLM inference process, enabling draft models to access semantic information from target models through cross-attention mechanism. We employ inverse RoPE transformation to eliminate positional encoding noise from KV cache, enabling effective fusion of multi-layer KV cache. Our multi-mask training strategy further enhances computational efficiency while reducing memory overhead. Experimental results on standard benchmarks show that KVSpec achieves comparable performance to EAGLE-3 while significantly improving training efficiency and reducing memory overhead. Additionally, KVSpec is deployment-friendly as it requires no modifications to target models or inference frameworks and operates through standard KV cache interfaces, making it a practical solution for speculative decoding applications.

DOI:10.1109/cbd63341.2023.00048.abstract: Recent deep learning relies on large-scale training of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), which can be time-consuming and computationally intensive. To improve DNN training efficiency, GPU clusters have been used to perform distributed training. However, distributed training has many limitations, including synchronization overhead in data parallelism, computational bottlenecks in model parallelism, and memory constraints in pipeline parallelism, all of which hinder training efficiency. Recently, hybrid parallel distributed training emerged as a solution. However, it doesn’t optimize the size of pipeline parallelism and data parallelism to further improve training efficiency. Our paper introduces HPopt, a method that combines data-parallel and pipeline-parallel training to enhance DNN training efficiency. We’ve designed a heuristic algorithm to improve scheduling decisions in hybrid parallelism. Experimental results on CIFAR-10 show that HPopt is 1.5 times faster than data parallelism and 4.3 times faster than Torchgpipe.

DOI:10.1109/ccai57533.2023.10201324.abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and the arrival of an aging population, the need for intelligent service robots is increasing. Older adults and the blind are susceptible to slipping due to weak vision, especially when they cannot see water on indoor floors. We use computer vision technology to solve this problem. However, it is challenging to detect floor water using existing target detection algorithms due to uncertainty about its shape and size. This paper proposes a floor water detection technology based on improved Resnet, which can be deployed on the intelligent service robot to remind the elderly and the blind to be careful When the service robot detects water in the ground. Our proposed topics and methods can significantly reduce the probability of the elderly and blind people slipping. The method proposed in this paper is 3.6% higher than the original Resnet18 and 8.1% higher than Mobilenetv2; the number of parameters in our method is only 8.5 percent of VGG16_bn and yet achieves similar performance to VGG16_bn. This paper suggests a new trajectory for intelligent service robots by detecting water on the floor, and it has demonstrated promising results in accuracy and speed. It is hoped that this paper will arouse more scholars’ interest in the detection technology of floor water.

DOI:10.1109/ccdc65474.2025.11090660.abstract: 3D object detection based on LiDAR point clouds is a pivotal technology in autonomous driving. Although Transformer-based algorithms achieve high accuracy, their quadratic computational complexity poses significant resource demands. Inspired by the evolution of state-space models, this paper proposes a novel 3D object detection algorithm based on Mamba-enhanced Grouped point clouds feature Extraction and Multi-Scale feature Fusion (M-GEMF). M-GEMF comprises two key modules: the dynamic sparse window Mamba module and the feature fusion module based on Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Mamba framework. The dynamic sparse window Mamba module uses a sparse window strategy combined with the Mamba layer to extract features, which improves inference speed and reduces memory usage. The feature fusion module integrates FFT and Mamba layers to strengthen feature extraction and fusion capabilities. Experimental results on the nuScenes and KITTI datasets show that M-GEMF achieves a superior balance between inference efficiency and detection accuracy, presenting an innovative approach to advancing 3D object detection.

DOI:10.1109/ccdc69976.2026.11560395.abstract: Accurate and real-time forest fire detection is essential for protecting ecological environments and natural resources. In complex real-world scenarios, fire and smoke targets often exhibit large-scale variations, irregular shapes, and strong background interference, which poses challenges to object detection models in terms of accuracy and robustness. To address these issues this paper proposes YOLO12-FS, an improved forest fire detection method based on the YOLO12 framework. First an SAConv2d module is introduced into the backbone network where switchable atrous convolution enables adaptive adjustment of the receptive field enhancing spatial modeling capability for fire targets at different scales. A DySample dynamic upsampling strategy is introduced during the feature fusion stage enabling the feature reconstruction process to adaptively allocate sampling weights according to feature content thereby improving detection performance in smoke dominated fire scenarios. Furthermore a Conv2Former detection head is employed to introduce global contextual modeling while maintaining the efficiency of convolutional operations resulting in more comprehensive multi scale feature representations. Experimental results on a forest fire dataset demonstrate that YOLO12-FS, integrating SAConv2d, DySample and Conv2Former achieves higher precision recall and mean average precision compared with the baseline model. The proposed method exhibits improved robustness and detection accuracy under complex backgrounds providing effective technical support for automated forest fire monitoring and intelligent early warning systems.

DOI:10.1109/ccet66260.2025.11199505.abstract: This paper proposes ECFMem (ElderCare: Fusion Memory Method), a novel memory management framework for large language models (LLMs) in elderly care scenarios. Inspired by the three-stage human memory model (sensory, short-term, and long-term memory), ECFMem dynamically partitions LLM memory into short-term memory-storing recent conversational inputs via attention key-value pairs in a temporary buffer-and long-term memory, which retains critical structured health/habit/relationship data as semantic triplets in an external vector database. To address fragmentation and coherence challenges in elderly dialogues, ECFMem integrates a trainable gating mechanism for contextaware memory fusion and introduces Token-to-Chunk retrieval to optimize short-term recall efficiency. Experiments on elderlyspecific datasets (e.g., EESID) demonstrate that ECFMem significantly enhances memory persistence and response relevance: LLMs augmented with ECFMem achieve up to 85.2% accuracy (a 21% absolute gain over baselines) in long-term health queries and sustain robustness through 1,500+ memory updates. This work bridges cognitive principles with LLM architecture, enabling proactive, personalized elderly companionship.

DOI:10.1109/ccgrid.2019.00053.abstract: On heterogeneous cluster systems, the convergence performances of neural network models are greatly troubled by the different performances of machines. In this paper, we propose a novel distributed Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) algorithm named Grouping-SGD for distributed deep learning, which converges faster than Sync-SGD, Async-SGD, and Stale-SGD. In Grouping-SGD, machines are partitioned into multiple groups, ensuring that machines in the same group have similar performances. Machines in the same group update the models synchronously, while different groups update the models asynchronously. To improve the performance of Grouping-SGD further, the parameter servers are arranged from fast to slow, and they are responsible for updating the model parameters from the lower layer to the higher layer respectively. The experimental results indicate that Grouping-SGD can achieve 1.2-3.7 times speedups using popular image classification benchmarks: MNIST, Cifar10, Cifar100, and ImageNet, compared to Sync-SGD, Async-SGD, and Stale-SGD.

DOI:10.1109/ccgrid.2019.00067.abstract: The recent rapid growth of the data-flow programming paradigm enabled the development of specific architectures, e.g., for machine learning. The most known example is the Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) by Google. Standard data-centers, however, still can not foresee large partitions dedicated to machine learning specific architectures. Within data-centers, the High-Performance Computing (HPC) clusters are highly parallel machines targeting a broad class of compute-intensive workflows, as such they can be used for tackling machine learning challenges. On top of this, HPC architectures are rapidly changing, including accelerators and instruction sets other than the classical x86 CPUs. In this blurry scenario, identifying which are the best hardware/software configurations to efficiently support machine learning workloads on HPC clusters is not trivial. In this paper, we considered the workflow of TensorFlow for image recognition. We highlight the strong dependency of the performance in the training phase on the availability of arithmetic libraries optimized for the underlying architecture. Following the example of Intel leveraging the MKL libraries for improving the TensorFlow performance, we plugged the Arm Performance Libraries into TensorFlow and tested on an HPC cluster based on Marvell ThunderX2 CPUs. Also, we performed a scalability study on three state-of-the-art HPC clusters based on different CPU architectures, x86 Intel Skylake, Arm-v8 Marvell ThunderX2, and PowerPC IBM Power9.

DOI:10.1109/ccgrid64434.2025.00038.abstract: In this work, from our trace-driven experimental measurements, we observed that despite employing homogeneous GPUs for distributed deep learning (DDL) training, stragglers persistently emerge, significantly prolonging time-to-accuracy (TTA) and squandering GPU resources. Previous approaches typically react to stragglers as they occur or are imminent during execution after scheduling, resulting in training delays before they are addressed and introducing additional overhead. To reduce the number of stragglers, this paper introduces a novel DDL training job scheduler for proactive straggler reduction (STRN), the first effort in mitigating stragglers during scheduling. STRN is devised based on our findings that various DDL jobs exhibit distinct sensitivities to straggling and a particular resource's overload, and the optimal synchronization strategy for a job hinges on its specific characteristics and operational environment. Thus, STRN assesses each job's sensitivity to each resource type and straggling. It aims to minimize the likelihood of resource overload for jobs with higher sensitivity to that resource and to ensure that jobs with higher sensitivity to straggling encounter less straggling. STRN initially runs a heuristic method and then transitions to a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based method once trained, facilitating expedited and optimal job scheduling. STRN also optimizes synchronization strategies for each DDL job to reduce overall TTA. Trace-driven real experiments demonstrate that STRN reduces average TTA by up to 59% and enhances average accuracy by up to 91% compared to state-of-the-art methods. We have made the source code available for distribution.

DOI:10.1109/cei66465.2025.11398460.abstract: Agricultural disease diagnosis requires accuracy, temporal consistency, and efficiency, yet existing deep learning models rely on single-frame analysis and ignore domain knowledge. We propose AgriMamba, a framework integrating closed-loop control theory with hierarchical temporal-spatial modeling. It introduces Agricultural Guided Control for knowledge-driven memory, TSH-Mamba for multi-scale temporal modeling, SMA for phenology-aware adaptation, and MAFF for multi-level feature fusion. On the Corn Disease & Stress dataset, AgriMamba achieves 91.7 % accuracy, surpasses state-of-the-art by 5.9 %, and reduces complexity and memory by 42 % and 38 %, establishing a resource-efficient paradigm for precision corn disease diagnosis.

DOI:10.1109/cgo68049.2026.11394842.abstract: The rapid growth in the size of deep learning models strains the capabilities of dense computation paradigms. Leveraging sparse computation has become increasingly popular for training and deploying large-scale models, but existing deep learning frameworks lack extensive support for sparse operations. Current approaches either require manual scheduling expertise or rely on exhaustive search taking hours to days, which are both incompatible with the interactive development essential to machine learning research. We present three algorithmic contributions that enable fast, automatic optimization of sparse tensor computations. First, we develop a heuristic-based loop ordering algorithm that avoids asymptotic performance cliffs while compiling in milliseconds rather than hours. Second, we introduce a tiling algorithm specialized for mixed sparse-dense computations that achieves performance comparable to hand-optimized kernels. Third, we present a format inference algorithm that automatically selects appropriate sparse tensor formats for intermediate and output tensors based on operation semantics. These algorithms are grounded in the computational properties of sparse tensor algebra, making them predictable and robust across diverse workloads. We implement these techniques in Scorch, a prototype sparse tensor compiler for PyTorch that demonstrates their practical effectiveness. With only minimal code changes, our approach achieves 1.05–5.80× speedups over PyTorch Sparse on end-to-end tasks including graph neural networks, sparse autoencoders, and sparse transformers, with compilation times fast enough for interactive ML development.

DOI:10.1109/cicn67655.2025.11368053.abstract: Medical image segmentation faces significant challenges in accurately delineating boundaries and preserving finegrained details, especially in complex anatomical structures and pathological regions. While U-KAN has demonstrated strong performance by integrating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) into the U-Net architecture, it still has two key limitations: insufficient feature recalibration across channels and space, and the inability of its convolutional decoder to model global context effectively due to fixed receptive fields. To address these issues, we propose CSKAN-U, a novel model that augments tokenized KAN with dual-channel and spatial attention mechanisms (the CSKAN block) and replaces the convolutional decoder with 2D Mamba decoder for efficient long-range dependency modeling. Our experiments on three benchmark datasets—BUSI, GLAS, and CVC-ClinicDB demonstrate that CSKAN-U significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving higher segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of KAN, attention mechanisms, and the Mamba decoder, validating CSKAN-U as an effective solution for medical image segmentation tasks.

DOI:10.1109/cisat71030.2026.11682188.abstract: Accurate vessel trajectory prediction is crucial for maritime traffic monitoring and safety. Transformers perform well, yet their positional encoding generalizes poorly to long sequences due to limited training lengths. We introduce a frequency-informed initialization using the FIK (Frequency-Informed Kinematic) schedule and predictive offset, providing a principled initial state. On Danish Strait and Brittany AIS datasets, our method reduces 4 h error to 1.7828 nm (19.2% over TrAISformer [1]), ADE to 1.0925 nm (13.7%), and FDE to 2.0866 nm (17.3%). The offset acts as a frequency compensator: when base frequency aligns with data, offset increases 15 h error by 22%; when mismatched, offset on standard sinusoidal encoding lowers 15 h error by 22%. Against eleven baselines, our method achieves SOTA for 4–8 h and reveals the long-horizon boundary of positional encoding. Significance tests (p<0.01) and cross-dataset validation at five-minute resolution confirm robustness and generalization.

DOI:10.1109/cisp-bmei68103.2025.11259236.abstract: Hyperspectral images, known for their nanoscale spectral resolution and extensive band coverage, are essential for various applications, including resource exploration and environmental monitoring. However, acquiring hyperspectral images presents several challenges. Traditional scanning methods often experience low sampling efficiency due to the limitations imposed by the Nyquist sampling theorem. Existing techniques, such as conventional compressive sensing and deep neural networks, face issues like high computational demands, sensitivity to noise, and spectral distortion, particularly in complex scenarios or at low sampling rates. In this paper, we propose HQS-net, a deep unfolding-based hyperspectral image reconstruction network. It integrates imaging physics with half-quadratic splitting-derived alternating optimization-using prior knowledge (image structure, spectral correlation) for constraints, then unfolds iterations into a network, achieving synergy of deep learning and physical models. This design enables stronger noise resistance by leveraging inherent data properties. Experiments show HQS-net outperforms others in reconstruction quality and noise resistance.

DOI:10.1109/cloud72782.2026.00021.abstract: Compute and memory resources in cloud environments are strictly managed and isolated by the control plane; in contrast, network resources lack equivalent management and isolation mechanisms. This best-effort treatment of networking leads to significant challenges for modern AI workloads, which have diverse and bandwidth-intensive communication patterns. Without fine-grained network resource control, these workloads suffer from interference, unpredictable throughput, and suboptimal cluster utilization. To address these issues, this paper demonstrates how network bandwidth can be elevated to a first-class, schedulable, and enforceable resource within Kubernetes, the de facto standard for cloud-native orchestration. We introduce a new scheduling capability that models network interfaces as allocatable resources and regulates bandwidth sharing through the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) framework, with enforcement implemented using the Hierarchical Token Bucket (HTB) mechanism. We evaluate the system using multitenant AI workloads derived from real-world communication characteristics with a simulation-based approach and validate the proposed enforcement strategy in a real cluster. Results show that the proposed two-level bandwidth allocation improves tenant performance predictability and satisfaction while maintaining packed cluster utilization.

DOI:10.1109/clusterworkshops61563.2024.0.abstract: Efficient utilization of multi-core processor architectures requires the development of parallel programs. However, achieving optimized parallelization remains challenging, often requiring specialized expertise and substantial development time. Various tools, including automatic parallelization techniques, aim to facilitate this process by analyzing source code and identifying parallelizable sections. Despite their utility, conventional tools relying on static analysis struggle to comprehensively handle all potential parallel patterns. In contrast, recent Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks, and have begun to be adapted to address software engineering problems. Leveraging this advancement, we propose an automatic parallelization approach for OpenMP framework using LLMs. Our method utilizes the CodeT5+ model, pre-trained on diverse programming languages, to analyze and parallelize C/C++ source code by generating OpenMP directives. To validate our approach, we trained the model on a dataset sourced from public GitHub repositories, focusing on implementations using OpenMP. Experimental evaluation focused on parallelizing benchmarks from the NASA Parallel Benchmark (NPB) suite demonstrates promising results: Among eight benchmarks evaluated, our approach achieved speedups comparable to manually parallelized codes in two cases, moderate speedups in three cases, and encountered a problem in effectively parallelizing one benchmark. Overall, our model successfully parallelized 73% of the loops in NPB, showing its potential to enhance productivity in parallel programming tasks.

DOI:10.1109/cogmi67134.2025.00022.abstract: Dispatchers (also referred to as emergency telecommunicators) are critical first responders who navigate high-pressure situations to ensure effective emergency response capabilities. Studies reveal that dispatchers frequently experience elevated levels of stress due to factors such as time-sensitive decision-making and insufficient organizational support, contributing to mental health challenges. While advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have demonstrated potential in emergency services, there is limited research applying AI tools to analyze the emotional well-being of dispatchers. Furthermore, there is a lack of discussion regarding potential biases and the adaptations that may be necessary for the successful implementation of such an approach. This study develops an AI-driven approach using natural language processing (NLP) to analyze stress through emotion detection, from audio recordings, laying the groundwork for future applications with dispatchers. Specifically, we compare five classifiers trained on publicly available emotional speech datasets (used as a proxy for emergency communications) in English and Spanish to explore their potential for aiding future mental health support for dispatchers. We find that the classifiers dealing with neutral and calm emotions are the highest performing and have the potential to align with real-world dispatcher scenarios, making it promising for practical adoption of this approach to detect emotional states for mental health initiatives. Through speech-based emotion detection, this AI driven approach offers a pathway toward understanding cognitive-affective states (or what one is thinking and feeling) in emergency telecommunications by capturing the emotional component and laying the foundation for future systems that could explore decision-making during calls. Overall, we demonstrate the potential of AI to support mental health in this high-pressure profession, contribute practical, industry-informed insights on bias and considerations surrounding real-world implementation, and promote early intervention and well-being for dispatchers.

DOI:10.1109/coins65080.2025.11125797.abstract: Neural processing units (NPUs) have become essential in modern client and edge platforms, offering unparalleled efficiency by delivering high throughput at low power. This is critical to improve the TOPS/W of the NPU, leading to longer battery life. While NPUs were initially designed to efficiently execute computer vision (CV) workloads such as CNNs, the rising demand to run transformer-based large language models (LLMs) locally now calls for significant architectural and software adaptation. This paper presents LLM-NPU, a comprehensive software-hardware co-optimization framework that enables scalable, power-efficient LLM deployment on NPUs under tight compute and memory budgets. We present software solutions such as vertical and horizontal operator fusion, quantization-aware weight compression, hybrid key-value (KV) quantization, eviction strategies, and static-shape inference that target memory bottlenecks and compute inefficiencies in LLM execution. On the hardware side, we explore domain-specialized NPU enhancements, including processing-in-memory architectures, extended input channel accumulation, structured sparsity acceleration, GEMM engine optimizations, mixed precision, microscaling format support, and fusion-aware execution pipelines. These co-designed innovations can collectively improve the energy, throughput, and latency of NPUs for LLM workloads.

DOI:10.1109/compsac61105.2024.00143.abstract: Recent research has shown growing interest in the arithmetic reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), especially those built on the Transformer architecture. However, our understanding of the intrinsic processes within these models for arithmetic calculations remains scant. This study leverages causal mediation analysis to offer an in-depth look at how Transformer-based LLMs approach complex arithmetic problems. We experimentally intervened on particular model activations and assessed the resulting shifts in prediction probabilities, allowing us to pinpoint which parameters are crucial for such reasoning tasks. We discovered that for complex arithmetic operations, information is channeled from mid-layer activations to the final token through enhanced attention mechanisms. Subsequently, Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP) modules synthesize this data, integrating it into the model's residual pathways. To validate these observations, we also evaluated the activation dynamics across different types of tasks, such as retrieving numbers from text and answering fact-based questions.

DOI:10.1109/compsac69091.2026.00432.abstract: Coordinating heterogeneous LLM agents under congested online settings is difficult because bursty task arrivals and limited per-agent capacity may induce hotspot overload and severe tail waiting time. This paper proposes an online scheduling method based on candidate-set contraction before assignment. Specifically, tasks are first routed through subscription matching to identify a task-relevant candidate pool, after which layered gating is applied to enforce capability feasibility, historical quality, and real-time load constraints. The remaining candidates are then ranked using a composite score that balances competence and load, with stable tie-breaking introduced to reduce assignment fluctuations under contention. We evaluate the method under a reproducible protocol with both regular and congested regimes. Across benchmarks covering code generation, arithmetic reasoning, and preference-based evaluation, the proposed approach preserves competitive task performance while reducing both mean and 95th-percentile waiting time in congested settings relative to representative linear, flat, and hierarchical baselines. The findings suggest that candidate contraction is a useful strategy for achieving more stable coordination in heterogeneous LLM-agent systems.

DOI:10.1109/concapan66820.2025.11512641.abstract: The increase in violence in urban areas has created an urgent need for systems capable of accurately identifying actions that endanger citizens. In this context, video surveillance systems supported by video anomaly detection approaches have served as a foundation for developing automatic solutions to identify unusual behaviors; however, most of these methods focus exclusively on detection and do not address the detailed classification of anomalies. This work proposes a modular framework for the joint detection and classification of Abnormal Human Actions, understood as anomalous actions caused by humans that pose a threat to public safety. The proposed approach, evaluated on an edge device, achieved an accuracy of $59.02 \%$ in Abnormal Human Actions classification, a detection rate of $80.0 \%$ on the UCF-Crime dataset, and a processing speed of 283.49 fps, demonstrating its potential for deployment in real-world, resource-constrained video surveillance environments.

DOI:10.1109/cros69211.2026.11565761.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising approach for executing long-horizon manipulation tasks from natural language instructions by reasoning over visual perception, linguistic context, and embodied actions. Building on vision language models, VLAs aim to generalize across tasks, objects, and environments while operating under real-world conditions. This paper presents an overview of the foundational principles underlying VLAs for generalist robotic manipulation. We review commonly used simulation frameworks and benchmarks, and categorize recent VLA architectures according to their action generation mechanisms. By providing a unified view of these topics, this work aims to clarify the current design space of VLA systems and identify trends and open challenges toward general-purpose robotic manipulation.

DOI:10.1109/cscwd68734.2026.11581548.abstract: Accurate short-term power load forecasting is pivotal for efficient energy management, grid stability, and operational cost optimization in modern power systems. However, existing deep learning models face a fundamental trade-off between capturing local temporal patterns and modeling long-range dependencies, limiting their forecasting accuracy and computational efficiency. To address this challenge, we propose a novel hybrid TCN-Mamba architecture that synergistically combines Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) for parallelizable local feature extraction with Mamba’s selective state space mechanism for efficient long-sequence modeling. Our framework achieves linear computational complexity while effectively capturing both short-term fluctuations and long-term temporal correlations in power load data. Comprehensive experiments on the UCI LD2011 2014 Dataset demonstrate that the proposed model consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines (BiLSTM, LSTM-Transformer, and CNN-LSTM-Attention), achieving the lowest MAE (0.0173) and NMAE (0.0204), with improvements of up to 14.36% and 17.41%, respectively. Ablation studies confirm that the TCN component enhances sensitivity to local temporal dynamics, while Mamba predominantly contributes to global dependency learning. These results validate that our hybrid architecture effectively balances accuracy, efficiency, and scalability, providing a robust foundation for intelligent energy management systems.

DOI:10.1109/cscwd68734.2026.11582248.abstract: Prompt-based learning has redefined interactions with language models, enabling precise guidance for desired information generation and unlocking novel applications of natural language understanding. However, in Event Temporal Relation Extraction (ETR), a core task, existing prompt methods suffer from unbalanced template capabilities, limiting performance. To address this, we propose an RDrop-based regularization-driven method to balance cross-template ETR capabilities and design the RC2ETR model. It integrates RDrop regularization with two distinct templates (using manually selected optimal modifiers) to identify effective combinations, achieving balanced capabilities and enhanced dual-template synergy. Experiments show that RC2ETR outperforms baselines overall, with balanced individual-label results.

DOI:10.1109/cvidl70130.2026.11638023.abstract: Early-exit networks reduce inference cost but lack risk-aware decision-making and reliable confidence estimation. We propose CAE2-CRC, a framework that reformulates early exiting as a sequential risk-adaptive decision process. It introduces a formally defined Calibration-Aware Reliability Score (CARS) whose two constituent terms-predictive certainty and confidence trustworthiness-are derived from first principles and jointly optimized via a Joint Calibration and Reliability (JCR) loss. A Bayesian Multi-Armed Bandit policy using Thompson Sampling enables dynamic threshold selection under both stationary and non-stationary reward conditions via a windowed posterior mechanism. Experiments on GLUE, T5, and BLIP-2 tasks show competitive accuracy with the highest speedup (1.85× on BERT-large), superior robustness, and statistically significant ECE reductions of up to 3.89 absolute points at shallow layers, which we formally link to improved final prediction accuracy via the JCR Reliability Alignment term.

DOI:10.1109/cvpr52729.2023.01138.abstract: Optimization in multi-task learning (MTL) is more challenging than single-task learning (STL), as the gradient from different tasks can be contradictory. When tasks are related, it can be beneficial to share some parameters among them (cooperation). However, some tasks require additional parameters with expertise in a specific type of data or discrimination (specialization). To address the MTL challenge, we propose Mod-Squad, a new model that is Modularized into groups of experts (a ‘Squad’). This structure allows us to formalize cooperation and specialization as the process of matching experts and tasks. We optimize this matching process during the training of a single model. Specifically, we incorporate mixture of experts (MoE) layers into a transformer model, with a new loss that incorporates the mutual dependence between tasks and experts. As a result, only a small set of experts are activated for each task. This prevents the sharing of the entire backbone model between all tasks, which strengthens the model, especially when the training set size and the number of tasks scale up. More interestingly, for each task, we can extract the small set of experts as a standalone model that maintains the same performance as the large model. Extensive experiments on the Taskonomy dataset with 13 vision tasks and the PASCAL-Context dataset with 5 vision tasks show the superiority of our approach. The project page can be accessed at https://vis-www.cs.umass.edu/Mod-Squad.

DOI:10.1109/cvpr52734.2025.00490.abstract: Multimodal 3D segmentation involves a significant number of 3D convolution operations, which requires substantial computational resources and high-performance computing devices in MRI multimodal brain tumor segmentation. The key challenge in multimodal 3D segmentation is how to minimize network computational load while maintaining high accuracy. To address the issue, a novel lightweight parameter aggregation network (SuperLightNet) is proposed to realize the efficient encoder and decoder for the high accurate and low computation. A random multiview drop encoder is designed to learn the spatial structure of multimodal images through a random multi-view approach for solving the high computational time complexity that has arisen in recent years with methods relying on transformers and Mamba. A learnable residual skip decoder is designed to incorporate learnable residual and group skip weights for addressing the reduced computational efficiency caused by the use of overly heavy convolution and deconvolution decoders. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a leading reduction in parameter count by 95.59%, the 96.78% improvement in computational efficiency, the 96.86% enhancement in memory access performance, and the average performance gain of 0.21% on the BraTS2019 and BraTS2021 datasets in comparison with the state-of-the-art methods. Code is available at https://github.com/WTU-MIS-Laboratory/SuperLightNet.

DOI:10.1109/cvprf71909.2026.00205.abstract: Omni-MLLMs have attracted growing attention for their potential to emulate human-like multimodal perception and reasoning. However, existing mathematical reasoning benchmarks are confined to text-only or text-image formats, lacking a comprehensive evaluation of omnimodal capabilities. Moreover, these benchmarks predominantly rely on textbook-style images that differ significantly from the diverse and unstructured visuals encountered in realworld educational and human-computer interaction scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose MathAll, a real-world multimodal mathematics benchmark encompassing text, image, and audio modalities. By incorporating hand-drawn images and explanatory audio, MathAll simulates authentic human reasoning processes and enables comprehensive evaluation of both modality-complementary and modality-integrated reasoning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that current Omni-MLLMs struggle to effectively handle cross-modal inputs, especially when modalities contain imperfect or ambiguous information, and consequently lag behind human-level reasoning. As input complexity increases, models experience difficulties in visual perception and audio understanding, exposing inherent limitations in modality coordination and generalization. Based on these findings, we propose several promising directions for future research and model enhancement.

DOI:10.1109/cvprf71909.2026.00817.abstract: State-of-the-art (SOTA) generative models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in image synthesis or text generation, often with a large capacity model. However, these large models cannot be deployed on smartphones due to the limited availability of on-board memory and computations. Quantization methods lower the precision of the model parameters, allowing for efficient computations, e.g., in INT8. Although aggressive quantization addresses efficiency and memory constraints, preserving the quality of the model remains a challenge. To retain quality in previous aggressive quantization, we propose a new fractional bits quantization (FraQAT) approach. The novelty is a simple yet effective idea: we progressively reduce the model's precision from 32 to 4 bits per parameter, and exploit the fractional bits during optimization to maintain high generation quality. We show that the FraQAT yields improved quality on a variety of diffusion models, including SD3.5-Medium, Sana, PixArt- $\Sigma$, and FLUX.1-schnell, while achieving 4 - 7% lower FiD than standard QAT. Finally, we deploy and run Sana on a Samsung S25U, which runs on the Qualcomm SM8750-AB Snapdragon 8 Elite Hexagon Tensor Processor (HTP).

DOI:10.1109/cvprf71909.2026.00866.abstract: The computational demands of visual tokens in Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) present a significant challenge for real-time inference, particularly in long-contextual scenarios. The Key-Value cache generated by these visual tokens requires substantial GPU memory, slowing down decoding speed. While existing KV cache compression methods have made some progress in language and single-image multi-modal contexts, there has been limited exploration in video-based multi-image scenarios. To bridge this gap, we conduct an in-depth analysis of the attention mechanism in MLLMs and identify an intriguing phenomenon termed “Attention Myopia”: the model inadequately allocates attention to later images, which impedes the direct application of existing compression methods to multi-image contexts. Based on this insight, we propose Dynamic Attention Subsidy (DAS), a novel technique that adjusts attention scores to ensure a more balanced selection of critical tokens. Additionally, to preserve the integrity of visual information, we propose a reclamation mechanism called “Recycling Bin”, which compresses the discarded tokens to a minimal size. Our method achieves around 1.5× speedup on inference in decoding phase with 20% of the KV cache footprint compared to the original model, while maintaining consistent performance across over 20 diverse datasets. Crucially, our technique is plug-and-play, allowing seamless integration with existing pre-trained MLLMs without incurring any additional training costs.
